episodes.179235: Thunderstorms developed across the Fox Valley along the lake breeze during the afternoon hours on Wednesday (5/31).  The strongest storms produced hail up to one inch.
episodes.179288: Daytime heating and moisture over eastern NM allowed storms to ignite over the Sangre de Cristo Mountains spreading southeast over the northeast and east central plains by the late afternoon to early evening hours. A few storms reached severe limits near Raton, Tucumcari, and Clovis. Storms moved east into Texas after 9 PM local time.
episodes.179311: An isolated severe storm produced a localized damaging downburst.
episodes.179319: Strong outflow winds were observed around Cheyenne from decaying thunderstorms in northern Colorado on the evening of the 31st.
episodes.179320: Numerous thunderstorms developed in far eastern Wyoming on the 30th organizing into a line of storms as they reached the Nebraska Panhandle with strong winds gusting 45 to 60 mph.
episodes.179323: Moisture increased across western Colorado ahead of the next Pacific system. This, paired with daytime heating, led to scattered showers and thunderstorms. The stronger storms produced gusty winds in excess of 58 mph across the Grand Valley.
episodes.179326: Continued very warm temperatures on an above normal snowpack resulted in excessive runoff leading to flooding across portions of west-central Colorado, particularly Gunnison County. Conditions were only exacerbated by heavy rain from thunderstorms in the days prior.
episodes.179391: A severe thunderstorm developed near Hermosa and tracked east-southeast through northern Oglala Lakota County. The storm produced large hail along its path.
episodes.179393: A severe thunderstorm in Nebraska clipped the Pine Ridge area, producing wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.179394: A cluster of strong thunderstorms developed into a line as they moved into south central South Dakota, producing small hail and wind gusts around 60 mph across portions of the area.
episodes.179408: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produced gusty marine winds across the Tampa Bay neighboring waters.
episodes.179428: An overnight storm complex moved across portions far western Oklahoma, producing a period of severe wind gusts near Arnett, OK. By the daytime, convection developed across central into northern Oklahoma on weak surfaces boundaries across the area. Severe-caliber wind gusts occurred with a semi-organized storm in northern Caddo County, Oklahoma.
episodes.179429: A line of storms developed in northeast South Dakota on the early afternoon of May 30th.  The strongest of the storms produced a wind gust of 60 mph at the South Dakota Department of Transportation Mesonet station 4 miles north of Altamont. Additionally, a trained spotter 6 miles north of Gary reported that the combination of wind and hail damaged beans crops and the plants in his garden.
episodes.179455: Sufficient lift ahead of an upper low over California and Arizona and Gulf moisture ahead of the dryline across eastern New Mexico allowed widespread showers and storms to initiate around midday. Several supercells produced large and severe hail along with two tornadoes in the central and south-central highlands of Guadalupe and Lincoln County. Later that evening, training supercells grew upscale into a convective complex with flash flooding across east central New Mexico.
episodes.179506: Strong thunderstorms developed along a weak frontal boundary. Large hail and gusty winds were reported.
episodes.179556: A line of storms developed in the late afternoon and evening in western South Dakota. As they proceeded east, this line of storms produced an estimated 60 mph wind gust 3 miles west of Okaton before weakening.
episodes.179605: A severe thunderstorm developed over the Custer area, producing hail to golf ball size across much of the area, with a few hailstones as large as baseballs.
episodes.179962: A band of thunderstorms developed around midnight from May 30th into the 31st from around Ord, southeastward to near Hastings. This activity developed in response to increasing low level jet ahead of a decaying cluster of storms that moved through western and central Nebraska during the evening hours of May 30th. Thunderstorms that developed over south central Nebraska were on the strong side, initially, and posed a marginally severe hail risk. The lone hail report was nickel size hail from far NW Adams County, though additional isolated pockets of dime to nickel size hail probably occurred between Kenesaw and Loup City. A band of scattered thunderstorms continued into the early morning hours of the 31st, but became weaker and less organized with time.
episodes.180249: Several severe storms produced large hail and damaging wind across Minnesota in the afternoon and evening hours of May 30th.
episodes.180505: The combination of outflow boundaries from convection developing near Cuba spreading north across the Straits of Florida and spreading southwest off the mainland of southwest Florida resulted in isolated gale-force wind gusts near the western Lower Keys.
episodes.180542: On the evening of May 30th, a line of thunderstorms developed in East-Central Colorado that moved across the region. Some of these thunderstorms produced hail up to quarters in size. Sub-severe thunderstorm wind gusts up to 54 mph were also observed along with heavy rainfall that yielded up to 4 inches of storm total precipitation during the event.
episodes.180637: A shortwave moving through the region led to the development of isolated thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 31st. Conditions were once again not favorable for severe storms, but one storm did produce penny-sized hail in St. Louis County.
episodes.180651: Thunderstorms developed over the Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of May 30th. As they tracked east into the eastern panhandle and western Sandhills, they became severe. Hail up to quarter size and thunderstorm wind gusts to around 70 MPH was reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.180799: During the late evening of the 30th a line of thunderstorms moved west to east through the combined Oklahoma and Panhandles. This initial line had a few severe storms embedded in them that produced some severe winds in Beaver County, OK of which did cause some wind damage. Nickel size hail was also initially reported in Moore County near Cactus, TX. After the initial line converged into a complex to the east several more scattered thunderstorms formed over portions of the western to central portions of the Texas Panhandle. One of these storms became severe dropping hail up to 1 in diameter over Randall County at 0518CDT on the morning of the 31st.
episodes.180800: During the late evening of the 30th a line of thunderstorms moved west to east through the combined Oklahoma and Panhandles. This initial line had a few severe storms embedded in them that produced some severe winds in Beaver County, OK of which did cause some wind damage. Nickel size hail was also initially reported in Moore County near Cactus, TX. After the initial line converged into a complex to the east several more scattered thunderstorms formed over portions of the western to central portions of the Texas Panhandle. One of these storms became severe dropping hail up to 1 in diameter over Randall County at 0518CDT on the morning of the 31st.
episodes.180801: Two different rounds of showers and thunderstorms overtook the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles on the afternoon and evening of May 31st. The wave of storms produced severe wind gusts between 58 and 60 mph through the northwest TX Panhandle  and portions of the Oklahoma Panhandle. The second wave of storms moved into the southwest TX Panhandle from eastern New Mexico later in the evening. These storms produced severe winds between 58 and 63 mph, as well as hail up to the size of nickels. They also were heavy rain producers which led to some urban flooding in the east side of Canyon, TX as well as portions of Amarillo, TX.
episodes.180802: Two different rounds of showers and thunderstorms overtook the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles on the afternoon and evening of May 31st. episodes.180841: Storms produced large hail and damaging winds across portions of southwest Kansas.
episodes.180858: A severe thunderstorm produced a brief wind gust to 59 mph in Sedgwick County.
episodes.180859: Severe thunderstorms produced wind gusts up to 70 mph in Weld County.  Several trees were knocked down and limbs were snapped.  A carport was also flipped over.
episodes.180958: A band of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon along a trailing boundary which extended from a subtle upper-level impulse that lifted from South Dakota into North Dakota.  A couple stronger cells in the line produced some penny- to nickel-sized hail.
episodes.181067: Numerous thunderstorms developed or moved into East Central Colorado during the evening.  Hail up to quarter size was reported with a couple of these storms.
episodes.181068: Widespread thunderstorm activity occurred over Northwest Kansas during the evening.  Hail up to golf ball size was reported at Rexford.  Thunderstorm winds moving out ahead of the storm over Cheyenne County caused a localized dust storm on Highway 27.  Later in the evening wind gusts up to 59 MPH were reported near Norton.  The repeated rounds of rainfall over part of the area led to flooding in western Wallace County.
episodes.181076: During the afternoon of May 31st, a cluster of thunderstorms produced locally damaging winds across parts of the Chicago metro as well as a landspout in west-central McHenry County.
episodes.181246: Heavy rain fell on May 31st leading to flash flooding in Miami and Leavenworth Counties.
episodes.181291: A shortwave trough near the Four Corners with an accompanying sub-tropical jet streak helped initiate afternoon thunderstorms across much of southeast New Mexico and far west Texas. Several strong to severe thunderstorms developed across this region. One particular thunderstorm developed into a left-moving supercell. This supercell produced a long-track swath of intense straight-line winds in Loving and Lea Counties causing large amounts of wind damage.
